action: Add a single-bone Armature to the scene.
notes: Creates the initial bone.

action: Enter Edit Mode on the Armature.
Enable In Front in the Armature's viewport display settings.
keys_or_menu: Object Properties > Viewport Display > In Front
notes: Makes the bones visible through the mesh.

action: Select the entire bone.
Move the selected bone upward.
Rotate the bone 90 degrees to the right.
Scale the bone down.
Move the bone into position around the hip.
notes: Position it where the hip joint should be.

action: Select the appropriate section of the bone for extrusion.
Extrude a bone downward to the knee.
Extrude another bone downward to the ankle.
Extrude two additional bone segments.
notes: The instructor does not clearly specify their destinations in the transcript.

action: Select the ankle bone and extrude a controller bone outward along the Y-axis.
notes: Creates the ankle/foot controller.

action: Select the knee bone and extrude another controller bone along the Y-axis.
notes: Creates the pole controller.

action: Select the ankle controller and clear its parent.
notes: Separates the controller from its original bone parent.

action: Move the ankle controller forward.
Select the knee controller and clear its parent.
Move the knee controller outward.
Switch to Pose Mode to inspect the bone positions.
keys_or_menu: Ctrl + Tab / Mode Selector > Pose Mode

action: Check whether the bones are positioned correctly relative to the mesh's left-right alignment.
notes: Move the bones horizontally if the mesh is not centered.

action: Enter Pose Mode.
notes: Repeated mention of the mode transition.

action: Select the first bone and Shift-select the second bone.
notes: The two bones are selected for IK setup.

action: Create an inverse kinematic constraint using the active bone.
notes: Creates the IK relationship.

action: Move the IK controller to test the rig.
notes: Demonstrates that the IK chain moves.

action: Move the controller to observe the knee twisting and bending.
notes: Demonstrates the pole-target problem.

action: Select all bones and clear their transforms.
notes: Resets the rig before further configuration.

action: Select the IK-controlled bone to configure its pole target.
Open Bone Constraints and use the eyedropper to assign the knee controller as the pole target.
Re-select the intended controller bone as the pole target.
notes: The spoken description is slightly unclear about the exact selection sequence.

action: Inspect the foot rotation caused by the pole-target assignment.
Reset the pole angle to zero.
notes: Avoids restricting the pole controller's movement through an unwanted angle offset.

action: Select the Armature object.
Enable the display of bone axes.
notes: Shows the X, Y and Z bone axes.

action: Inspect the IK bone's X-axis direction relative to the pole target.
notes: Identifies the expected axis orientation.

action: Switch to Edit Mode and inspect the bone's X-axis orientation.
notes: The X-axis is not pointing toward the pole target.

action: Keep the pole angle at zero and correct the bone orientation in Edit Mode instead.
notes: The instructor explains why changing the pole angle is not the preferred solution.

action: Select the bone and adjust its roll until its X-axis points toward the pole target.
Set the bone roll to 90 degrees.
notes: The exact sign may depend on the Armature setup.

action: Select the other relevant bone and set its roll to 90 degrees.
notes: Aligns its X-axis toward the pole target.

action: Return to Pose Mode.
Select the relevant bone and rotate it to check whether the foot follows.
notes: Demonstrates that the foot does not yet follow correctly.

action: Prepare to correct the foot controller's rotation and parenting relationship.
Enter Edit Mode, select the relevant bone and clear its parent.
Select the controller bone and parent the previously selected bone to it while keeping its offset.
Parent the other relevant bone to its controller while keeping the offset.
keys_or_menu: Shift + Click > Ctrl + P > Keep Offset

action: Return to Pose Mode and inspect the bone's rotation and position.
notes: The rotation now works, but the position is incorrect.

action: Select the affected bone and open its Bone Constraints settings.
Add a Copy Location constraint to the selected bone.
Assign the shin bone as the Copy Location constraint's target.
notes: The instructor mentions selecting the shin bone near the knee.

action: Set the Copy Location constraint's Head/Tail value to 1.
notes: Makes the constraint use the bone's tail position.

action: Rotate the bone and check that it stays in the correct position and follows its controller.
notes: Tests the parenting and Copy Location setup.

action: Move the controller downward to check that the foot follows it.
Move the pole controller from side to side to test the knee's bending direction.
notes: Verifies that the pole target works.

action: Switch to Object Mode to prepare for binding the mesh to the Armature.
Select the mesh first and then Shift-select the Armature.
notes: The Armature must be the active object.

action: Parent the mesh to the Armature using automatic weights.
keys_or_menu: Object > Parent > Armature Deform > With Automatic Weights
notes: Creates the mesh's automatic skin weights.

action: Inspect the mesh deformation after binding it to the Armature.
Switch to Pose Mode.
Select the main controller bone and move it to test the rigged mesh.
Move the foot controller and check that the mesh and foot deform correctly.
Rotate the controller around the Z-axis to rotate the leg.
notes: Demonstrates the final rig functionality.
